s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei on microscopic examination

raw.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz

differentials: ewing sarcoma of the external ear canal

shortlist.label: acoustic neuroma
shortlist.why_kept: gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and sensorineural hearing loss

shortlist.label: middle ear choristoma
shortlist.why_kept: mass in the ear canal and expansion of the fallopian canal and stylomastoid foramen

shortlist.label: cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: mass in the ear canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal

shortlist.label: otosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: hearing loss and abnormal bone growth in the middle ear

raw.rationale: The presence of a nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, expansion of the fallopian canal, and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal, along with the gross examination showing a specimen consisting of cartilage and microscopic examination revealing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, are consistent with a middle ear choristoma, which is a rare benign tumor that can cause facial weakness and hearing loss.

rejected.label: acoustic neuroma
rejected.why: Acoustic neuroma typically presents with hearing loss, tinnitus, and imbalance, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: facial palsy
rejected.why: Facial palsy is a symptom rather than a diagnosis, and it does not explain the presence of a mass in the ear canal or the imaging findings.

rejected.label: cholesteatoma
rejected.why: Cholesteatoma is a type of skin cyst that can cause destruction of surrounding bone, but the microscopic examination in this case shows cartilage and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, which is not consistent with cholesteatoma.

rejected.label: otosclerosis
rejected.why: Otosclerosis is a condition that affects the middle ear and causes hearing loss, but it does not typically cause facial weakness or a mass in the ear canal.
